newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO slide seen stem by crude gains.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO slide seen stem by crude gains.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices may see short term support from crude gains but the market remained oversupplied, traders said on Monday.

NYMEX February crude on ACCESS was last traded at $26.30 per barrel, up 21 cents from New York while Brent climbed 4 cents at $24.38. Crude futures were supported by cold weather sweeping across the U.S northeast.
Traders said the current price slide may be stem by firm crude prices.
They said regional demand remained poor.
"Chinese demand remained weak," said a trader.
Cash prices for end January loading supplies were quoted at $118-$120 per tonne on Monday.
In the swaps market, front-month January was last quoted at $115.75/$116.75 per tonne, down from Friday's quotes at $116.25/$117.
